Review this change for security vulnerabilities.

Changed files (you may Read these and any other file in the repo):
  - metadata/app-info/en-US.json
  - metadata/version/0.2.0/en-US.json

Unified diff (only + lines are new):

=== DIFF: metadata/app-info/en-US.json ===
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+{
+  "name": "Hey Reachy",
+  "subtitle": "Control your Reachy Mini",
+  "privacyPolicyUrl": "https://github.com/alexey1312/reachy-mini-swift/blob/main/docs/privacy.md"
+}


=== DIFF: metadata/version/0.2.0/en-US.json ===
@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+{
+  "description": "Hey Reachy is a native client for the Reachy Mini Wireless desktop robot — one app for iPhone, iPad and Mac.

REQUIRES A ROBOT

Hey Reachy talks to a Reachy Mini Wireless on your network. Without one the app stops at its Connect screen, because every feature lives behind a live session with the robot's own daemon. There is no demo mode and no account to create.

WHAT IT DOES

• Connect — find the robot by Bonjour, type an address by hand, or reach it from outside its network through the Hugging Face relay. Robots are identified by hardware id, so the same robot at a new address is still the same robot.

• Live control — joystick teleop of the 6-DoF head, the antennas and body rotation, with the robot's camera and two-way audio, so you can talk through its speaker.

• 3D viewer — a RealityKit model built from the robot's own URDF and meshes, mirroring it in real time.

• Moves — browse and play the recorded moves the robot ships with, from the app or by asking Siri for one by name.

• Apps — install, update and remove robot apps from Hugging Face Spaces, following each job as it runs. The robot wakes itself before an app starts and parks again when it lets go.

• State — the control loop's frequency, worst interval and error count charted live, beside the robot's own processor, memory, temperature and uptime.

• Files — an SFTP browser for the robot's filesystem.

• Bluetooth setup and recovery — put a brand-new robot onto Wi-Fi over an encrypted Bluetooth channel, or bring back one that fell off the network.

AT HOME ON YOUR DEVICES

Widgets for the Home Screen, the Lock Screen and StandBy. Control Center power controls. Siri and Shortcuts for waking, sleeping, powering off, launching an app or playing a move — and each of those can name which robot it means, so two Reachys on one desk are told apart. Six accent themes, each with a matching app icon.

PRIVACY

Nothing is collected. The app talks to your robot on your own network and, if you choose to sign in, to Hugging Face with your own account. There is no server on our side.

A NOTE ON YOUR NETWORK

The robot's daemon provides no authentication and no encryption of its own. Use Hey Reachy on a trusted private network or on the robot's own access point — never through a port forward or a public address.

Hey Reachy is unofficial and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Pollen Robotics. It is an independent client for the robot daemon's documented HTTP and WebSocket API. "Reachy Mini" is a product name of Pollen Robotics, used here solely to describe what this app is compatible with.

Requires iOS 18 or macOS 15.",
+  "keywords": "robotics,robot,teleoperation,telepresence,remote control,urdf,servo,bonjour,webrtc,sftp",
+  "promotionalText": "Joystick teleop, the robot's camera and two-way audio, a live 3D twin, recorded moves and the robot app store — for the Reachy Mini Wireless on your desk.",
+  "supportUrl": "https://github.com/alexey1312/reachy-mini-swift/issues",
+  "marketingUrl": "https://github.com/alexey1312/reachy-mini-swift"
+}


Investigate per the method in your instructions, then return the findings list.

content.text:
Both changed files are static App Store Connect metadata (app name, subtitle, description, keywords, and three URLs) consumed by the `asc` release tooling to populate the app listing. Content is developer-authored strings and HTTPS links to the project's own GitHub repo — no attacker-influenceable input, no runtime sinks, no code paths introduced.

Nothing in the diff reaches a shell, filesystem, network, template, or auth sink; the URLs are all `https://github.com/alexey1312/reachy-mini-swift…` and the privacy-policy URL currently 404s (a listing-quality issue, not a security issue). No control regressions, no gate/action mismatches, no registry fanout implicated by metadata strings.
